trial_court: Court of learned Judicial Magistrate Kullu, District Kullu, H.P.
case_name: Smt. Kala Devi vs Shri Mehar Singh And Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: Shri Mehar Singh and Ors., respondents

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner-applicant filed an application under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. She claimed protection order, residence order, and monetary relief. She alleged that her husband started demanding money and beating her after she expressed inability to fulfill demands.

legal_principles.principle: To claim benefit of the Act, 2005, a couple must be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage, including being unmarried.
legal_principles.held: They must be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage, including being unmarried and they must have voluntarily cohabited and held themselves out to the world as being akin to spouses for a significant period of time.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
cited_cases: D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal, (2010) 10 SCC 469
keywords: relationship in the nature of marriage

legal_principles.principle: A man maintaining a woman financially and using her mainly for sexual purpose or as a servant is not in a relationship in the nature of marriage.
legal_principles.held: It would not be a relationship in the nature of marriage.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
cited_cases: D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal, (2010) 10 SCC 469
keywords: relationship in the nature of marriage

legal_principles.principle: To prove a relationship in the nature of marriage, evidence must show that the couple held themselves out to society as being akin to spouses and were otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage.
legal_principles.held: The couple must hold themselves out to society as being akin to spouses, they must be of legal age to marry, they must be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage, including being unmarried, and they must have voluntarily cohabited and held themselves out to the world as being akin to spouses for a significant period of time.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
cited_cases: D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal, (2010) 10 SCC 469
keywords: relationship in the nature of marriage

legal_principles.principle: A person cannot claim benefit of the Act, 2005 if they are not legally qualified to enter into a legal marriage.
legal_principles.held: She cannot be said to be legally qualified to enter into a legal marriage, which she subsequently solemnized with respondent No.1.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
cited_cases: D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal, (2010) 10 SCC 469

outcome.final_order: The applicant was granted protection order, residence order, and monetary relief.
